Mr. Mollah comes for a first visit and describes a sudden high fever, severe aching in the bones and muscles, and pain behind the eyes. He is an accountant and his symptoms started during the monsoon after mosquitoes bred in water tanks near Cumilla. He has Hypothyroidism. He explains that the fever came on suddenly with severe bone and muscle pain, and that the pain behind his eyes is worse when he moves them. He has had no nosebleeds, no bleeding gums, and no black stools. He has not taken ibuprofen or aspirin, though he has used paracetamol for the fever. He reports no rash, no vomiting, and no belly pain. He has no history of dengue before and has not travelled outside Cumilla recently. He says he has been drinking less fluid than usual because of the fever, and he feels weak. On examination: platelet count 132000 per microlitre, temperature 101.3°F, BP 115/77 mmHg, pulse 103 bpm, weight 56 kg. There is no rash and no bleeding. Assessment: Dengue fever. Plan: a prescription was issued. He was advised to drink at least three litres of fluid a day, avoid ibuprofen and aspirin, repeat the platelet count in 48 hours, and go to hospital at once for bleeding gums, black stools, or severe belly pain. Follow-up in 48 hours with a repeat platelet count.
